newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steadies after hitting nine-month low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steadies after hitting nine-month low.

text.p: IPE Brent crude steadied on Thursday to close above fresh nine-month lows posted in afternoon dealing but brokers said weak fundamental and technical factors pointed to further losses to come.
May Brent closed 32 cents lower at $18.19 a barrel, representing a modest recovery after plunging as low as $18.07, a level not seen since June 25 last year.
"There was a bit of shortcovering in the pit but technically we've broken down and with the fundamentals looking weak it should go lower again," said a broker.
Oversupply was weighing heavily on Brent, dealers said.
The prompt futures contract has lost 25 percent of its value in three months as North Sea, Middle Eastern and West African availability has improved.
Winter demand has fallen away and the U.S. gasoline season is looking less than promising, brokers said.

While predicting U.S. summer gasoline demand would grow by 1.8 percent this year, the Energy Information Agency (EIA) forecast production during the second and third quarters would increase by 2.2 percent.
"The Brent-gas oil crack has been improving but WTI-gasoline is the spread to watch," said a broker.
The spread between NYMEX crude and gasoline futures on Wednesday dipped below $6 a barrel for the first time in a month and has shed about 90 cents in the last week.
April IPE gas oil closed earlier $3.50 a tonne lower at $162.00 in quiet trade, posting narrower losses than predicted. Much of the decline came in the last hour of trade.
"Nothing really went on, it was a pretty boring day in a market looking for headlines," said one gas oil futures broker.
